existing_larger_budget_control.interpretation: The same HTTPX multi-version query is complete at 1200 for the baseline but incomplete at 2400. Project is incomplete at both. More budget is not an observed repair.

principled_next_directions.direction: Keep global as the default; project remains an explicit experimental ranking policy.
principled_next_directions.reason: The registered no-regression gate fails on three evidence-loss configurations and twelve first-source configurations. Small aggregate gains and future latency improvements cannot waive that gate.
principled_next_directions.next_validation: No source change in this analysis. Any promotion requires separately frozen development work and a fresh untouched holdout after that work is complete.

principled_next_directions.direction: Handle explicit version/source selectors independently of recency and generic lexical popularity.
principled_next_directions.reason: Historical questions lose their intended older source while newer-source questions also lose to older material. A universal newest-source rule cannot satisfy both directions.
principled_next_directions.next_validation: Register new metadata-qualified cases across several version syntaxes and config formats, including unknown or ambiguous selectors; never hard-code these repositories, tags or gold values.

principled_next_directions.direction: Measure preselection candidate recall separately from final page selection and excerpt coverage.
principled_next_directions.reason: Two losses show a gold-bearing page disappearing from the returned top five while other pages of the same original source remain. candidate_count=11 is unchanged, but full candidate identities are not logged.
principled_next_directions.next_validation: On new development inputs, preserve bounded candidate IDs/ranks and selected page IDs plus query-facet coverage. Evaluate source-level/page-level diversity and field coverage without silently increasing the frozen context budget.

principled_next_directions.direction: Make excerpt selection respect complete source-local bindings and test evidence retention as budgets vary.
principled_next_directions.reason: The HTTPX gold page stays at rank two but its excerpt moves away from the required binding. The new excerpt is longer, so this is not merely insufficient total budget. The already saved 2400-character response also omits it; baseline itself becomes worse at the larger budget.
principled_next_directions.next_validation: Use new documents to test span/anchor preservation and budget nonmonotonicity, with exact offsets and whole config bindings. Preserve earlier budget outcomes; do not select a budget merely because it passes these known questions.

principled_next_directions.direction: Treat project-local scoring as a change of retrieval policy, separately from an optimization that preserves global scoring semantics.
principled_next_directions.reason: Default candidate_global is score-identical to the baseline, while the same candidate project mode changes rankings. Scores from different statistics scopes are not calibrated confidence values and are not numerically comparable across scopes.
principled_next_directions.next_validation: Define whether a future method prioritizes corpus-independent project ranking or exact compatibility with global corpus statistics. Test that policy on new independent sources and report the trade-off rather than claiming both by default.

limitations: This analysis only reads original saved responses, original-page follow-ups, comparisons, manifests and ingest receipts. It performs zero retrieval calls, zero new source-page API reads and no runtime/evaluator/source/gold edits.

The full preselection pool, component scoring terms and alternative excerpt-window objective values were not captured. Output-stage disappearance and reordering are observable; their precise internal stage is not proven.

All three newly lost evidence configurations use adaptive segmentation, but the source snapshots and observed page bodies remain valid. The observation is a ranking/selection/packing interaction with the 36-page adaptive corpus, not proof of a segmentation-data-loss bug.
The fifteen configurations concern six query IDs over four projects. Budgets, turn/session grouping and two text backends are repeated observations, not thirty independent failed questions.

The four missing-field questions still return related context in all twenty-four configurations per runtime/scope/backend. No calibrated abstention or general repository-wide absence claim is supported.
Questions are evaluator-authored over authentic official packaging files. This is not a production conversation sample or a coding-LLM task-success evaluation.

The first holdout attempt remains a valid observation of the frozen candidate. Once these failure details influence another implementation, these cases become development evidence for that implementation; a new untouched holdout is required for an independent generalization claim.
No causal latency or resource conclusion is made; the performance experiment is separate and continues unchanged.
